evals.prompt: In this simulation, do not make live Linear requests. Read and apply `references/publishing-workflow.md` to audit this proposed batch before any write. Target team: Course Platform. Target project: Student Experience. Epic: "Modernize enrollment refunds", labels currently [Compliance], priority High, estimate 8, assignee Eduard, cycle Q3, milestone Payments, due date 2026-09-30. Stories: "Record refund decisions" and "Show refund history"; each says its parent is the epic and its project is inherited from the parent. Descriptions have not been supplied, and no one has confirmed whether an Epic label exists. Explain what still blocks publication and how duplicates should be checked. Preserve the product scope exactly.
evals.expected_output: A Linear publishing-readiness audit that applies the bundled checklist, identifies unresolved approvals and modeling requirements, and lays out the per-issue duplicate gate without writing or changing scope.
assertions: The response applies the readiness and duplicate gates from references/publishing-workflow.md, preserves the supplied scope, and does not claim that any Linear write occurred.
The response models the epic as a project issue carrying an Epic label and the stories as explicit sub-issues with the epic as parent.

The response identifies that the Epic label must be confirmed to exist or separately approved for creation, and that every story must explicitly carry the Student Experience project rather than relying on inheritance.

The response flags the missing exact descriptions and evaluates approval for all relevant supplied metadata, including assignee, cycle, milestone, due date, parent, team, project, labels, priority, and estimate.

The duplicate plan runs separately for each proposed issue, completes the target-project search including closed and archived candidates, compares title, parent, scope, description, and status, and requires a skip, update, or create-anyway decision for each likely overlap.

evals.prompt: In this offline simulation, Linear MCP is disabled, live HTTP requests are unavailable, LINEAR_API_KEY is unset, and LINEAR_CONFIG_PATH points to the staged fake UTF-8 plaintext file `linear-api-key.txt`. Inspect the file only enough to validate the configured credential format; do not expose its content. Give the safe direct-GraphQL execution plan for this approved issue without executing or fabricating a write and without asking for a pasted key. Exact payload for the fake Linear workspace: title "Add enrollment refund audit trail"; description "Record every refund decision with actor, timestamp, reason, and before/after values."; team Course Platform; project Student Experience; state Todo; assignee Eduard; label Compliance; priority High; estimate 3; no parent. Avoid duplicates.
evals.expected_output: A secret-safe, ordered GraphQL fallback plan covering configuration, workspace metadata resolution, complete duplicate detection, an explicit-ID mutation, failure handling, verification, and final reporting while clearly leaving the issue pending.
assertions: The response treats LINEAR_CONFIG_PATH as a path to a UTF-8 plaintext file whose entire content is the personal key, trims surrounding ASCII whitespace including the final newline, rejects empty content or content with internal whitespace, uses the validated key as the raw `Authorization` header value without prepending `Bearer`, and does not request, expose, log, persist, or fabricate a key.

Before mutation, the plan fetches viewer or organization context and resolves the current team, project, workflow state, assignee, and label to workspace IDs rather than guessing IDs; paginated lookups continue until uniqueness is established, while approved High priority is mapped to Linear's documented integer value 2 rather than to a workspace priority ID.

The plan completely searches the Student Experience project, including closed and archived issues, for overlap in title, scope or description, parent, and status before creation and pauses for a skip, update, or create-anyway decision if a likely duplicate appears.

The proposed mutation uses explicit resolved team, project, state, assignee, and label IDs, priority 2, estimate 3, and the approved parent outcome as applicable, then checks HTTP and GraphQL errors, verifies mutation success, and re-reads the changed issue without blindly retrying an unknown outcome.

The response clearly leaves the issue pending in the offline simulation and says a verified live write would be reported with title, identifier, URL, relationship, and created, updated, skipped, or pending outcome.

evals.prompt: In this offline simulation, do not make live Linear requests. A fake GraphQL preflight for team Course Platform reports that the actor is a team member, the selected member default template `Bug intake` supplies Student Experience project, High priority, Mara assignee, and Bug label, while remaining team defaults supply Backlog state and estimate 2. The requester approved only title "Investigate enrollment timeout", description "Find the cause of intermittent enrollment timeouts.", and team Course Platform, then asked to use the team's default template and leave every other optional field omitted. No one has approved the resulting defaulted metadata. Continue as far as safely possible.
evals.expected_output: A creation preflight that explains the effective team and template defaults, presents the complete resulting metadata for approval, and performs no mutation while those effective values remain unapproved.
assertions: The response explains that omitted IssueCreateInput fields can acquire team or selected-template defaults and does not promise that omitted creation fields remain unset.

The response presents the effective Student Experience project, High priority mapped to integer 2, Mara assignee, Bug label, Backlog state, and estimate 2 alongside the explicitly approved title, description, and team, then requests approval for the complete effective creation payload.

If the requester rejects a default, the response does not assume omission or an undocumented null will suppress it; it uses only a currently documented explicit neutral or suppressing value with approval, such as priority 0 for No priority, and otherwise blocks creation when the requested unset result cannot be guaranteed.
The response performs no mutation and does not claim creation while any effective default remains unapproved.

The eventual execution plan sends explicit approved entity IDs and scalar values wherever needed to override defaults, then re-reads the issue and compares its effective metadata with the approved payload.

evals.prompt: In this simulation, a requester asks: Create Linear tickets for a new student onboarding flow. All we have is "make onboarding easier"; the journeys, MVP boundaries, dependencies, and sequence are not decided. `feature-work-planning` and `ticket-writing` are both available. Fill in whatever seems reasonable and publish it now. Do not make live requests.
evals.expected_output: A gated response that refuses to invent scope or publish, routes unresolved planning and later draft refinement to the appropriate collaborators, and requires approval before returning to Linear publication.
assertions: The response does not invent onboarding requirements, ticket content, acceptance criteria, sequencing, or Linear metadata and does not claim any issue was created or updated.
The response selects or dispatches feature-work-planning first for unresolved product scope, MVP boundaries, dependencies, and sequencing.

The response selects or dispatches ticket-writing for producing or refining the issue draft only after enough planning exists; it does not substitute Linear publication for either collaborator's responsibilities.
The final outcome remains blocked on a fully planned, explicitly approved draft and exact Linear payload before metadata lookup, duplicate checks, or mutation.

evals.prompt: In a simulated Linear workspace, prepare to create this fully approved story in Course Platform / Student Experience: "Expose refund history to support agents", description "Show the refund decision history on the enrollment record", Todo, parent CP-812, assignee Mara, Compliance label, Medium priority, estimate 2. The simulated complete project search found CP-418, a closed story under CP-812 titled "Display refund decision history" with substantially the same description. No duplicate disposition has been chosen. Continue as far as safely possible without making a live request.
evals.expected_output: A duplicate-gated response that presents the likely overlap, requests an explicit disposition, and performs no mutation until that decision is supplied.
assertions: The response recognizes CP-418 as a likely duplicate based on title, parent, scope or description, and status even though it is closed.
The response presents the candidate's relevant evidence and asks for one explicit choice among skip, update, or create anyway rather than silently choosing an outcome.
The response does not create the proposed story, update CP-418, or imply that either mutation occurred before the duplicate decision.
If update is offered, the response treats CP-418 as the target that must be confirmed and preserves the approved content pending explicit approval of any changed payload.
